title: Molten Aluminum-Induced Corrosion and Wear-Resistance Properties of ZrB<sub>2</sub>-Based Cermets Improved by Sintering-Temperature Manipulation.

recollection.intervention: Variation of sintering temperature during fabrication
recollection.structure: Likely densified ZrB2-based cermets with possible changes in grain size and phase distribution
recollection.mechanism: Higher sintering temperatures may improve densification, reduce porosity, and alter microstructure, leading to improved corrosion and wear resistance against molten aluminum
recollection.results: Presumably, cermets sintered at optimized higher temperatures showed lower corrosion rates and better wear resistance in contact with molten aluminum, possibly quantified by weight loss or depth of attack measurements.

score.note: The recollection identifies sintering-temperature variation and broadly connects improved densification/reduced porosity with better corrosion and wear resistance, but it is speculative and omits the SPS temperature range, 1500 °C optimum, binder pore-filling, 1600 °C binder loss, and all numerical results.
